name: Les Nubians
notes: The Franco-Cameroonian wing — "the lane's most explicitly African-rhythm entry". `confidence` is **low**: the research rates the entry medium-low and says the idiom and the language practice are sourced but "tempo, drum and harmonic detail are lane inference and marked". The one instruction the entry gives is structural and is followed exactly: "programmed kick/snare with the backbeat on 2&4 under a hand-percussion ensemble (djembe, congas, talking drum, shakers) that carries the actual rhythmic information in cross-rhythmic 6-over-4 or 3-over-4 patterns. Model the percussion as a separate, denser layer than the kit." So this is the only model in the section whose percussion density (5–9 a bar across five lanes) exceeds its kick and hat densities combined, and whose percussion gain offset is 0 dB — the kit is the accompaniment. The raised `tresilloBias` is the 3-over-4 cross-rhythm expressed in the one field that can carry it. Harmony is "minor-mode modal vamps with m9/m11 colour; harmony is static across long sections, with movement supplied by the percussion and the vocal counterpoint rather than by chord change", hence `maxChords` 2, a vamp harmonic rhythm and 8-to-16-beat chord durations. The melodic identity is "two-sister close harmony in parallel thirds and fourths — the lead is rarely alone", which is a call-and-response structure with the densest counter in this batch. ⚠ Every drum, melody and bass number here is INFERRED. ⚠ `countermelody.fillGapsOnly` is left inherited even though the entry says the lead is rarely alone, because turning it off makes the counter a second lead and trips the coherence check. ⚠ **`chords.harmonicRhythm` gained `syncopated_cell` (2026-08-17, harmony variety floor).** The entry says "minor-mode modal vamps with m9/m11 colour; harmony is static across long sections, with movement supplied by the percussion and the vocal counterpoint rather than by chord change". `chordDurationBeats` is the only parameter carrying a loop length, and it was **dead here**: `generators::chords::layout` reads it under `syncopated_cell` alone, which this model did not author — so every generation was one 4-bar hold instead of the documented loop. The sonority itself does not move: over a single-chord family every cell is the same chord re-voiced. ⚠ The cell range [8, 16] was already authored here. "Static" survives - the inherited single-chord family holds one sonority - and what the cell adds is the re-voicing, not a chord change.
